analysis.evidence: אֵלֶּה refers back to מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי נֹחַ, “the families of Noah’s sons.” The preposition marks those families as the source from which the nations spread after the flood.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and,” the preposition מֵ means “from,” and אֵלֶּה is a common plural demonstrative pronoun.

analysis.evidence: וּמֵאֵלֶּה (“and from these”) points back to the families of Noah’s sons. The plural subject הַגּוֹיִם identifies the nations that branched out from those families after the flood.
analysis.morphology: Niphal perfect, third person common plural, agreeing with the following subject הַגּוֹיִם.

analysis.evidence: הַגּוֹיִם is the subject of נִפְרְדוּ, “separated.” וּמֵאֵלֶּה, “and from these,” traces the nations back to the families of Noah’s sons after the flood.
